plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked dose-response & latent-period chart from Portier & Richet (15 February 1902, C. R. Soc. Biol. 54: 170–172) contrasts an untreated dog surviving >2.0 cc/kg of actinia toxin for days against a primed dog (22 days after a tiny first dose) suffering fatal shock within 25 minutes from just 0.10 cc/kg (a >20-fold drop in lethal threshold).

Biol. 54: 170–172) contrasting an untreated dog surviving >2.0 cc/kg of actinia toxin for days against a primed dog (22 days after a tiny first dose) suffering fatal shock within 25 minutes from just 0.10 cc/kg (a >20-fold drop in lethal threshold)
teach_overlay.scale: a dose twenty times too small to hurt a first-time animal became lethal in minutes on the second visit — because the danger wasn't the jellyfish poison anymore, it was the body's own counter-attack
